request.spec: Exports taken while a preview date is set use the preview figures.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Exports taken while a preview date is set use the preview figures.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored

agent.result_text:
The app already did what this request asks, so I didn't need to change any code. I ran `bin/e2e` on the untouched code first, and all 4 tests in `e2e/specs/acceptance.spec.ts` passed (4 passed, 2.2 min).

**Why it already works:** the people and claims exports build their CSV in the browser from figures the screen has already worked out. Those figures are calculated on `session.figureDay()` — the preview date when one is set, otherwise the sheet's today. Setting or clearing a preview also re-reads the sheet. Before writing a file, each export waits for the screen's requests to finish (`session.settled()`), so it never uses old figures. The main test checks this: a due of 10.00 becomes 11.00 in both exports while a 2026-05-01 preview is set, and goes back to 10.00 once the preview is cleared.

**My only edit** was to the comment above the export buttons in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`. It now says that an export taken while a preview date is set has the preview figures; before, it only mentioned the as-of date. I didn't re-run the tests after this change because it touches nothing but a comment.
